# OLYMPUS v0.0.26, "Bang, then go": the build sheet

Written 2026-11-19 for the round's four implementers (A to D) and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on **v0.0.25 as integrated** ("Hold to hold": F124 to F137, `GAUGE_LAST` 137, house-done group P, 429 rows, `test-zerocqb` in the Wreck and on the Tests menu, last): checked against the integrator's snapshot `.run/v026/v025-snapshot.tree` **10b699aa** (a patch on the v0.0.24 tag, rewritten after the menu switch; its first write 7d33dfbd differed in that one line of `scenes.js`) and `.run/v025/integrate.md` (§14 below lists every correction). The build starts on v0.0.25's tag and not before; where the tag differs from the snapshot, the code decides, stage 0 says so in `.run/v026/lead.md`, and the role adapts.

It is merged from three lens notes, all in `.run/v026-design/`: **defenders.md** (the role-players' brain, **DF§n**), **scene.md** (the scene, the bang, the lane, **SC§n**) and **carried.md** (what v0.0.24 and v0.0.25 leave open, **CA§n**, items **K1** to **K5**, **I1** to **I4**). Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections cited, then the lens notes ("as designed" means their mechanism, constants and tests stand unless this sheet changes them). Where the two play lenses disagree, the simpler one wins unless the play needs the other (the user's rule, below); every such choice is settled in §0. My own choices are marked (my call).

## The release in a page

ROADMAP §4.2's row 0.0.7f, `test-breach` "Bang, then go" (COMBAT §7.10, §7.11, §11.4, §25.18; VIEWS §3.4, §7.4, §7.7): one room of the Wheel's house 1 at 1 G, two role-players in marking-round kit running the defender's procedure, who **choose** (fight, cover, freeze, give up) by their felt band and their Nerve on their doctrine's table; the bang's window and the cost of a slow stack; the poses daze, cower and hands; the hit card on people, "Search him" and the hot wash's truth. The road is the user's: "now to bring this gameplay smoothly to CQB room clearing in full G, then ship CQB in microgravity and grav boots, and to real combat with enemies" (2026-11-08), and the order of 2026-11-17 (the overhaul, the anywhere round, then 0.0.7e "Hold to hold", 0.0.7f and 0.0.7g).

**The one idea** (both play lenses agree; my call): "Bang, then go" is **a new scene, not the live lane grown and not a new engine.** It is a `scenes.js` entry `'test-breach'` on the scenario `'test-shoothouse'` (as `'test-shoothouse-live'` is), whose fill is `shoothouse.js testShoothouse` with one new option, `breach`: the lane cut to its first leg, **room 1 of lane A as set**; v0.0.19's two role-players put in that room, one in each marine's sector, both on the card `fight`, so whatever they do after is §7.11's table and nothing else; the bang (the `flash` loadout) and whether the door is held, drawn from the seed; the lane ended at room 1's "Clear!". Everything else is the house as it stands: the tower, your #2, the bundles, T, the pars, "Flash it" and "#2, bang it", ON THE BANG and BANG TO ENTRY, the live side, `opfor.js`'s brain, `would.js`, the hit cards, the run sheet, the hot wash, "Again as …".

**Why not the live lane grown**: "Stack and clear, live" keeps its four pins (`house-live-pin`), its nine save points, F38 to F46's baselines and F44's balance (v0.0.22's question 15, still the user's) untouched; a three-room lane takes 3 to 4 minutes, while the bang's lesson needs repetition (one room: 50 to 70 s real on Again, SC§3). **Why room 1**: it is COMBAT §25.5.1's reference room within 0.3 m (the men 4.1 m from the threshold), so §25.18.2's computed window applies as printed; it is centre-fed, so each marine has his own man and your #2's work is half the scene; it is the lane's first door, 4.9 m from the start.

**What is new, exactly** (the rest is reuse, §0 item 1's table):
1. The scene, its URL `&breach=<bang|quiet>,<held|loose>`, `createGame({ breach })`, the draw `drawBreach`, the lane cut to room 1 and its end (B).
2. Room 1's two posts (`BREACH_SPOTS` 1a, 1b) through the seam that already exists (`rpStandsOf`, `spotOf`), and the held start: your man laid on the door from GO (A).
3. §7.10's one term, **a friend seen falling**: +10 on the other man's pool and −0.1 on his resolve, which `nerveCheck` already reads (A).
4. **The challenge ends a freeze**: Challenge offered on a man read COWERING; a frozen man who sees or hears it within 6 m gives up at its end (A).
5. **DAZED**: a shocked man (startled, stunned or flash-blind) read DAZED on the plaque, drawn in the `daze` frame on the stage and the card, by one helper (A's read, C's look).
6. **The window**: one record, one reader (`bangWindowOf`) for the card's WINDOW and THEIR CHOICES rows, the run sheet's "DOOR OPEN n S BEFORE THE BANG" and the hot wash's first line (B).
7. **"Search him"**: one optional 20 s row after "Clear!", behind a splash, that turns the man's card from belief to truth (A's row, B's wait, C's card).
8. The stage's `daze` and a real `cower` frame, from a numbered sample set the user scores (C).
9. "Another door" on the end card: a new seed, a new draw (B).

**The narrowest brain**: one room, one door, two men, one doctrine (Star Helix security, the table as built), the one dash; no blind fire, no flight, no throw, no hand to hand. Blind fire and the cell's doctrine wait for 0.0.7g's irregulars (§0 item 3).

**Before the roles, stage 0 (the lead)** records every pin, takes about 19 s of CPU off the quick suite with a test-only memo, fixes house-pace's seeds, and makes and sends the one new sample set on day 1.

**The roles**: **A** the defenders; **B** the scene and the lane; **C** the look; **D** the carried fixes. **Merge order**: stage 0, D, A, B, C (§7).

**Ship rules** (my calls):
- Stage 0 and D ship when F147 (nothing moves, but D's named re-records) is green.
- `test-breach` is on the Tests menu, after "Stack and clear, live", when F138 and F147 are green; else by URL only (`menu: false`, v0.0.25's switch), and the announcement says so.
- The look ships at `breach-poses`' defaults (D-a, C-a) until scored, said in the announcement.
- The cut line, if the round must shrink: "Another door" first, then "Search him" (the hot wash's truth stays). The rest is the row.

**The user's rules over every section**: "keep things simple, it's a game. I love the attention do detail, but only if it won't impact gameplay or performance (or introduce so much complexity it creates bugs)" (2026-11-19); "forget voice synthesis, no voices." (2026-11-19: every line is a text bubble at its speaker); the look chosen from numbered samples the user scores, the rated sets collapsed at the bottom of the gallery (2026-11-19); "we shouldn't know what's behind closed doors or walls without looking" (2026-11-19); "Paintball should end if the hit is 'fatal'" (2026-11-16); "enemies are NPCs and they run their own procedure to eliminate us ... Suppression, training and exprience will decide how well NPCs can respond to threats and whether they fight back, try to rush for cover or flee all together" (2026-11-07, COMBAT §7.11's source); test scenes explain nothing beyond their goal line (2026-11-06); one quantity, one helper; visuals obey the sim; AZERTY labels on physical codes.

**Kept as built and starred**: "Stack and clear" (★ 2026-11-17) and every pin of v0.0.25 (F147), but for the re-records named in §2 and §8, each with its cause; F1 to F137 never loosened.

**Rules of the round**: as v0.0.25's, with `.run/v026/` for patches and handoffs (it survives a reboot), `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v026/<role>/` for scratch, worktrees `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v026-<role> v0.0.25` with `node_modules` linked and `.run/v026/stage0.patch` applied, removed at the end. Four roles at `JOBS=2` each, `JOBS=1` while the user plays (input idle under 5 minutes, not the server alone); heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet run. A quick file under 3 s × k of CPU. No role commits; the lead integrates and releases.

**Ports**: A 8230, B 8231, C 8232, D 8233; reviews 8235 and 8236; the lead 8239; the runner's 8240 to 8249. Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first**: each role writes §3's exports as stubs, fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's export until that role merges. Every stub returns today's answer where `R.house.bangGo` is absent, so a stubbed role moves nothing.

**Integration**: the stage-0 tree the base; each patch cut against the tree the merges before it left (A on D's, B on A's, C on B's), applied with `git apply --3way` in the merge order; after each, `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs`, `'env-noregress ›'` and the house pins (`house-pin`, `house-live-pin`, `house-pin-drawn`, `zerocqb-pin`).

### The items, as built (the lenses' mechanism stands but for what is said here)

1. **The scene** (B; SC§0, SC§9, SC§11). `?play=test-breach`, seed 48213 at 10:00 unless `&seed`/`&hour`, `&tier=` the house's six sheets (the picker's five, the corporal by URL; the private by default), `&breach=<bang|quiet>,<held|loose>` (either part `*` or absent: drawn), `&setup=go` only (at GO; every other setup dropped with a toast). `&draw`, `&house`, `&layout`, `&rooms`, `&plans`, `&loadout` and `&opfor` dropped with one toast, "Bang, then go is played in room 1 as set." (the Wreck's way of v0.0.25: `core/debug.js` `BREACH_DROPPED` and `breachChoice` beside `SHIP_DROPPED` and `shipChoice`, chosen at `main.js`' URL house choice as `recURL?.ship` chooses `shipChoice`; and the fill drops them as `testShoothouse`'s Wreck branch does, so a test's `createGame` cannot pass them either). The house's lane: the brief (its own lines, SC§10.1), the sterile check, LOAD, MAKE READY, Standby, GO, room 1, "Clear!", the search offer, Stop, UNLOAD, SHOW CLEAR, the hot wash, the card. **The lane cut**: the stands made are room 1's only (1a, 1b: no turner, dummy or hall target past it); the legs are made as today, so every reader of `H.rooms` and `H.hall` keeps its shape, and the legs after room 1 stay `'ahead'` and are never opened; `legView`, the card, the ghost and house-done's readers list the played leg only (`state !== 'ahead'`). `R.house.bangGo = { v: 1, bang, held, code, window: null, track: {}, search: null }` is written on this lane only ("absent means default": no other save gains a key). **Not `R.house.breach`**: that key is taken, the house's breached doors by door id since v0.0.18 to v0.0.19 (`burst.js` the cut charge's `H.breach[o.id]`, `bundle.js` the R-7's ballistic breach `H.breach[door]`), so a flag read there would turn room 1's stands on mid-lane on any lane whose door was cut or shot. The fill writes `R.house.opfor` 'live' on this lane (`testShoothouse`' live line reads room 2's and 3's cards, which this lane has not), the scene's code in `bangGo.code`. The legs' due and the stall rules hold as on the house.
2. **The bang** (B, as built; SC§2, SC§4). `bang` gives both marines the `flash` loadout (`loadout.js`' preset, as `&loadout=flash` does), `quiet` the standard; room 1's door bundle starts with its bang variant at `flash` when issued (T below rung 2: "Flash it", then the DI's "Bang! Go." and the entry; from rung 2 one press, "Clear it, with the bang. Your corner: left."); the player may cycle it to "No bang". Measured on today's code (SC§2, room 2's man as the proxy): with the G-11, 0 casualties and no round from the man in the bang's room on 36 of 36 lanes; without it, a casualty on 8 of 8 recruit and private lanes by the keys and 7 of 24 from the corporal up. ON THE BANG by sheet: the recruit by the keys 1.93 to 1.99 s (inside `BANG_LATE_MS` 2 s by a hair: the recruit's teaching, no constant moved), the private 1.81 to 1.92, the corporal 1.44 to 1.59, the sergeant 1.09 to 1.16, the Raider and the tier one 1.06 to 1.12 s.
3. **The slow stack** (B; SC§4, DF§4). Three clocks, no new constant: the door's leaf to your entry, the bang to your entry (past `BANG_LATE_MS` 2 s the fault, past `FLASH_BLIND_MS` 5 s the bang wasted), the door open before the bang (the throw and the fuse: a cue the man spends turning to the door). A man looking away is laid on the door again 1.0 to 2.1 s (his startle) + 0.3 s (`TURN_MS`) + about 2.2 s (`aimMsOf` from low ready, 2,230 ms at 5.73 m) after the bang [DF, computed]; in room 1 at 4.1 m `breach-window` prints it. The slow stack costs little in his choice (his pool falls 2 points a second after its 1.5 s grace) and much in his hands.
4. **The held door** (A's start, B's draw; §0 item 4). `held` puts **one man, 1a (yours, the far left corner)**, at GO in `st 'aim'`, his carry aimed, his head and rifle on room 1's threshold (`aimAt` [29.0, 11.7]), `L.cue` the door, his aim already laid: a marine through the door in his sector is taken in as `'sector'`. 1b is loose (`st 'wait'`, face 'up', the door outside his 110° cone), as is 1a when `loose`: the door's leaf turns them. Because the door opens 2.7 s (tier one by T) to 5.7 s (recruit by the keys) before the burst, a loose man has turned to the door when the bang lands, and it blinds him as it blinds the held man (§25.18.2's "doorbell"). So with the bang, held or loose changes little; without it, the held man fires first on nearly every low-sheet run (SC§2): **the quiet held door, one seed in eight, is the scene's hard case**, and the card says afterwards "THE DOOR WAS HELD".
5. **The choice** (A; SC§6, DF§4). The procedure as built (`opfor.js`'s steps 1 to 9) on the security table as built (`CHOICE_TABLE`): calm or under fire (0 to 44) fight, no roll; suppressed (45 to 69): a pass fights, a miss covers, bad or disaster freezes; pinned (70 to 100): a pass covers, a miss or bad freezes, a disaster surrenders with a marine's weapon within 5 m, else freezes; rolled at a band change, the first moment after a shock, and after `CHOICE_DWELL_MS` 1.5 s still suppressed or worse from cover or a freeze; a choice holds; surrender is final. **New**: `friendDown` (§3.1). What it gives [DF, computed by d20 enumeration, the second man's roll as his friend is paired and down]: one bang leaves a security-grade man at felt 47, 44 or 41 at hardening 13, 16 or 19 (mostly 16), the top of "under fire", so **one bang alone does not reach his choice; the bang's value is the startle and the eyes**. With his friend down and an entry at 1.5 s, his felt is 50 to 56: fight 60 to 65%, cover 25%, freeze 10 to 15%. Without a bang he always fights (felt 6 to 12). **Two bangs** ("#2, bang it" as well) pin him: cover 45 to 50%, freeze 45%, surrender 5 to 10%.
6. **Read, not told** (A's read, C's look; SC§6.4, DF§6). One map, in this precedence: down (or ruled out sitting): `sit`, DOWN; giving: `drop`, `handsUp`, `handsKneel` (H1, scored), HANDS UP; **shocked** (his block's `startleUntilMs`, `stunUntilMs` or `blindUntilMs` after now), not down or giving: **`daze`, DAZED** (new); frozen: **`cower`** (the stage draws the kneel today; a real frame now), COWERING; the dash: `run`, RUNNING; aimed: `aim`, AIMING; at his hide: `crouch`, LOOKING; waiting or turning: `stand`, LOOKING. The plaque's word is written only on a passed identification (`contact.js identify`), never from the record; the stage draws only what you see (v0.0.23's rule); the daze is drawn exactly while the sim's block says so, so **the player sees the window close**: the man straightens, turns, and the rifle comes up. One helper, `men.js liveStateOf(state, T, ms)`, is read by the identification, the card's words, the instinct, `opforLook` (the Seen record's frame) and the stage's frame. **The stage does not read `opforLook`** (its readers are `people/seen.js` and the tests): it draws a live man from his actor through `arms/look.js gunLook` (a view-readable module, `SIM_FOR_VIEW`, which already imports `scenarios/shoothouse.js`) and the view's figure loop; so the stage's `daze` and `cower` come from `gunLook` (`action.frame`, as its P-12 admin branch sets the admin's frames) reading `liveStateOf`, and the figure loop's line beside the hands' (`a.hands === true` → `handsUp`) only if a carry-free frame needs the bare look.
7. **The challenge** (A; DF§5). Challenge (`'contact:challenge'`, `CHALLENGE_MS` 1.2 s, "Show me your hands!", as built) is offered on a man read COWERING (today: 'unseen', 'hands', 'phone' only). A man in `st 'freeze'` or `'cover'` challenged by a marine within `KNEEL_M` 6 m whom he sees (`men.js bodySeen` from his eye) or hears (`supp.js hearsVoice`; deaf after the bang, the gesture still reaches him if he sees it) gives at the challenge's end (`startGive`, then the kneel at once). Unchallenged, a frozen man whose felt falls back under 45 (about 4 s after the last input) rises and fights the marine covering him: §7.11, and the reason T offers "He's done. Challenge him." first. A cowering man still holds his rifle: a round at him is lawful and not faulted.
8. **The window** (B; SC§5). `breachWindow(state, H, now)` at the end of `liveTick`, on this lane only, writes `R.house.bangGo.window = { bangAtMs, doorAtMs, inAtMs, twoInAtMs, men: { [key]: { dazeToMs, blindToMs, onDoorAtMs, downAtMs, gaveAtMs } } }` on transitions only, and pushes each man's `[ms, st]` to `R.house.bangGo.track[key]` when his `st` changes (and his choice with its band and grade when `L.choice` changes): O(1) a tick, about ten entries a man. `bangWindowOf(state)` is its one reader (not `windowOf`: `contact.js` has a module-private `windowOf`, the take-in's window, which A edits beside). The card: "THE WINDOW: BLIND TO 5.0 S · YOU IN AT 1.92 S · YOUR #2 AT 2.40 S", a line a man ("1A: DAZED TO 1.8 S · BLIND TO 5.0 S · DOWN AT 2.9 S"), "THEIR CHOICES: 1B COVER AT 2.1 S (SUPPRESSED, NERVE MISSED)"; quiet, "THE DOOR: 1A ON IT BEFORE IT OPENED · YOU IN AT 1.40 S". The run sheet keeps "ON THE BANG" / "BANG TO ENTRY" and adds "DOOR OPEN n S BEFORE THE BANG" over `DOOR_OPEN_SAID_MS` 3 s (shown, not faulted). The hot wash's first line, `windowWords(state)`, SC§10.3's five; a casualty's lesson by cause still leads.
9. **"Search him"** (A row, B wait, C card; §0 item 7). After room 1's "Room clear!", each **accounted** man (`men.js accountedOf` 'down' or 'hands') offers **"Search him · 20 s"** within `SEARCH_M` 1.5 m (out of reach the keys walk you; T's offer is the row with its walk beat, the bundle's `move` as built); the instructor says "Search them if you want the truth now." once, and his "Stop." waits `SEARCH_OFFER_MS` 6 s for a search to start, then comes as built. Pressed, the lane's end waits on it (`R.house.bangGo.search = { key, untilMs }`), its `SEARCH_MS` 20 s pass behind the house's skip with the splash "Searching him: 20 s", and at its end `T.live.searched = { by, atMs }`, the fact 'house' `{ phase: 'rp', kind: 'searched' }`, and **his card shows the truth** (`marks.js hitMarks(..., { phase: 'truth' })`), "SEARCHED" and the would-have's verdict ("WOULD HAVE BEEN FATAL: THE CHEST", "A WOUND: THE ARM", "HIS PANEL STOPPED ONE"). **A needs**: v0.0.19's brain as built; nothing of B or C. A's `rpStandsOf` and `spotOf` branch reads `rangeOf(state)?.house?.bangGo`, which only B writes: A tests on `rpScript` (a bare state with `R.house.bangGo` set by hand) until B merges.

**B needs**: A's seam (`BREACH_STANDS`, the held start, `liveStateOf`, the search row, `L.choice`'s band and grade), stubbed until A merges (a stub `rpStandsOf` returning room 1's two stands where `breach` is set).

**C needs**: A's frame names (`daze`, `cower`) and `liveStateOf`; B's scene for `ui-breach`; v0.0.25 D's `prepareOwn`; the user's picks (defaults until scored). C merges last: its browser case plays the whole scene.

**Merge order**: stage 0, D, A, B, C. `GAUGE_LAST` 149 at C's merge with every row homed; `tests/breach-done.mjs` a filter of house-done after it. The two roles in `main.js` (B's `newGame` and "Another door") and none other: the lead merges it.

## 9. Acceptance: what the user must feel

1. **The Tests menu's "Bang, then go"**: the goal line; the instructor's bubbles on the catwalk, "Room 1, live: two role-players with marking rounds, playing Star Helix security. Masks stay down. A fatal hit ends it. Put them down or take their surrender." and "You each carry a G-11. On the bang, go." (or "No bangs today. Speed is your bang."); nothing about the door.
2. **The bang**: "Flash it" (or one T from the corporal up); the door, the throw, the bang; both men in the daze, a hand to the eyes, the plaque "CONTACT · RIFLE · DAZED · TAKEN IN 0.80 S"; you in, "ON THE BANG 1.6 S".
3. **They choose**: your man down, "Hit!"; the other sees him fall and fights on, takes cover, cowers, or drops his rifle, "Don't shoot!", hands up. Never the same twice for no reason, and the card says why ("1B COVER AT 2.1 S (SUPPRESSED, NERVE MISSED)").
4. **The cower**: "He's done. Challenge him."; challenged, he gives up and kneels. Left alone, he comes back up and fights.
5. **The slow stack**: hold at the door 3 s after the bang and the man's rifle comes back onto the door as you watch his daze end; "BANG TO ENTRY 3.0 S. You gave them back the bang."
6. **The quiet held door**: your man's rifle is on the door before it opens; he fires first unless you are very fast; the card says "THE DOOR WAS HELD", the wash "He had his rifle on that door before you opened it. That is what the bang is for."
7. **"Search him"**: 20 s behind a splash; his card turns from what you believed to what was, "SEARCHED · WOULD HAVE BEEN FATAL: THE CHEST".
8. **The card**: THE WINDOW, THEIR CHOICES, the paint and the would-have, the truth cards; "Again as …", "Again", "Another door"; a run 50 to 70 s real on Again.
9. **Carried**: T acts on the first frame after you load a save at a pause; in the Wreck, your #2's "Got you." and "Through." a bubble at the scuttle, not a line in the radio box (K6; the brace itself is v0.0.25's).

**For the integrator** (as v0.0.25's): F147 after stage 0 and each merge; `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each; the gauges never loosened (`'house-flawless-quick ›'`, `'house-flawless-keys ›'` all MET); `game-upgrade` loads every save to v0.0.25's; F60, F148 and `?bench=breach` PASS on a quiet machine, the user judging Windows; a browser smoke on :8239 (`?play=test-breach&tier=private&breach=bang,held` by the keys to the card; `&tier=sgt&breach=quiet,loose` by T; `&setup=go` on another seed; Search him once; no page error, console error or failed request; the server killed after); the heavy suites once on a quiet machine after the last merge (`env-noregress`, `breach-nodead`, `breach-pin`, `ui-breach`, the house pins, `house-flawless-live`, `house-pace`, `GATES=1`'s four, v0.0.25's heavy suites); `house-done` with every row F1 to F149.
